name: PT Buma Internasional Grup Tbk

frontmatter.title: BUMA Internasional Group: fees from coal, debt from a producer
frontmatter.summary: BUMA is a coal-mining contractor carrying producer-sized debt. We rate the shares BUY with a Rp187 target. The base case floors at zero because enterprise value sits below net debt; the positive value is the bull branch, and the branch clears the debt on capital intensity, not on a margin recovery. The associate stake decides BUY rather than HOLD.
thesis: Revenue is a fee for moving rock and coal, not a coal price: lower thermal prices hit customer performance and contract negotiations rather than revenue directly [S2, p.32], so we model volume and renewal timing, not a price realisation.
The debt is the investment case: FY2025 finance cost of US$91.6m exceeded free cash flow to the firm, and the shortfall is refinanced every year rather than repaid [S6].
EBITDA is US$173.8m on the LK's own lines — operating result plus total depreciation and amortisation — reconciling to the US$175m the company reports [S2, pp.10, 362, 405-407].

The DCF puts enterprise value at US$306.5m, below net debt, so the base and the bear floor at zero; the bull branch, 15.0% of the mass, is worth Rp1,382 and carries the target. It clears the debt on the capex ratio, not on the margin recovery [S0].

The peer EV/EBITDA cross-check is retired: the data packs' EBITDA field is an EBIT field, and rebuilt on the peers' own LK depreciation the corrected multiple values DOID's equity at zero [S0, S2, p.362].

The associate stake at book is optionality, not solvency: on a full write-off the bull branch stays positive and the target falls just above the price, so the add-back decides BUY versus HOLD [S0, F55].

catalysts.event: Next covenant test; waivers were obtained for the two prior dates [S6, p.77]
Full-year 2026 results, the FY2026 covenant pack and any dividend decision
Clearmatch insurance funding facility matures; the current sukuk and bond portion falls due
Syndicated bank facility matures, five and three-quarter years after the December 2023 first drawdown
Adaro South Tutupan contract expiry; the only dated client expiry inside the forecast

blocks.text: **What changed.** The construction, not the wording. First, the bull's value is now attributed to its actual driver: the branch clears the debt on the capex ratio, not on the margin recovery. The engine's own grid shows the two mirrored operating shocks alone leave the twelve-month value at the floor, and the capex shock contributes almost all of the branch's equity [S0]. That is stated in the scenario and in the valuation and risk sections, with its source — capex between the ratios the company actually spent in FY2023 and FY2024, below FY2025's [S2, p.72] — rather than credited to the margin story. Second, the associate sensitivity is corrected: the bull equity is positive before the associate is added, so a full write-off does not floor the branch, it moves the target from BUY to HOLD. The previous version had that backwards [S0, F55]. The peer-multiple retirement and the D&A double-count correction from the prior round stand. The earlier target was not an engine output: it was a hand adjustment to the branch weight, and the engine run that preceded the pack refresh already printed SELL on the same inputs.

We rate DOID BUY with a twelve-month target of Rp187, 40.3% from Rp133. It is one of Indonesia's largest coal-mining contractors, but the equity sits behind a debt load the operating cash flow does not cover, so the valuation is a view on whether enterprise value can outgrow the debt [S2, S6].

FY2025 revenue was US$1,480.3m, EBITDA US$175m, finance cost US$91.6m and net loss US$-127.6m, with parent equity of US$51.6m against net debt of US$872.7m [S2, S6]. The DCF at 11.9% produces enterprise value of US$306.5m, below net debt, so the base and the bear floor at zero; the bull branch, 15.0% of the probability mass, is worth Rp1,382, and it is the entire positive value [S0].

That is the honest shape of a levered equity: the base case at 60.0% is worth Rp0 because enterprise value does not clear the debt, the bear at 25.0% is worth the same for the same reason, and the target of Rp187 is the probability-weighted value after the 10.0% haircut [S0]. The call turns on the bull's weight and on its capital intensity. The weight is anchored to the house base rate for this archetype, annualised to a twelve-month branch and shaded for the covenant risk a producer does not carry; the exact arithmetic, including the weight at which the target equals the price, is written out in `fund record`, where it can be audited [S0, S6, p.77]. The capital intensity is sourced to what the company has actually spent [S2, p.72; S6, p.10]. A sustained margin recovery, an award that lifts volume without new capital, or a refinancing that cuts the interest burden would change the call; a debt-for-equity converts the bull into a zero for existing holders [S6].

DOID became a coal-mining contractor through the acquisition of PT Bukit Makmur Mandiri Utama, still known as BUMA, then bought Downer's Australian mining-services business and Atlantic Carbon Group; it now trades as PT BUMA Internasional Grup under the old Delta Dunia identity [S2, p.60]. The revenue model is a service fee: BUMA removes overburden, drills, gets coal, hauls and manages mine infrastructure, paid per unit of work under multi-year contracts [S2].

In FY2025 it moved 439 million bcm of overburden and produced 84 million tonnes of coal at a stripping ratio of 5.2x, below FY2024's 545 million bcm and 90 million tonnes [S2, p.13; S5]. First-half FY2026 revenue was US$459.8m from Indonesia, US$210.7m from Australia and US$22.3m from the United States, and the top five customers were 78.0% of revenue [S6, pp.106, 117].

The book is long-dated but finite: Adaro South Tutupan, started in April 2026, delivers 239 million bcm and 44 million tonnes to end-2030 [S4], while the Australian contracts run to mid-2030 and September 2027, then become renewals [S2, p.49]. Atlantic Carbon owns more than 8,000 hectares [S2, p.366], and the company holds 22.6% of an ASX-listed copper associate, up from 20.0% [S6, p.67]. Northstar Tambang Persada controls 38.2% with a free float of 45.5%, so any capital-structure solution is negotiated [S2, p.88; S0].

Indonesian coal is a volume business with a policy overlay: the FY2026 RKAB is 600 million tonnes of permitted production against expected output near 720 million, and the domestic market obligation requires producers to sell 25.0% of output locally [S9]. For a contractor the RKAB sets how much rock clients may move; royalty changes hit the producer's willingness to strip, not the fee, so we model no royalty line.

Thermal coal corrected while metallurgical coal and copper rose; the company states lower thermal prices did not directly reduce revenue but affected customer performance and negotiations [S2, p.32]. The coal price reaches DOID through the client's willingness to strip and the rate negotiated at renewal, not a realisation per tonne, so we put no coal price in the model; volume is the driver, and FY2025 overburden and coal production both fell, on weather and on contracts concluding at Broadmeadow, Commodore and Saraji [S2, p.13; S5].

Competition is among contractors with national fleets: the barriers are fleet capital, a safety record and working capital to carry receivables through a ramp [S2], but the moat is narrow, since the owner can move the work at the end of a term [S5]. Buyer power is high with the top five customers at 78.0% of revenue [S6, p.106], and rivalry at renewal leaves a thin spread over a heavy asset base.

Revenue fell from US$1,553.7m in FY2022 to US$1,480.3m in FY2025, -15.7% year on year, and gross margin fell from 13.1% and 13.4% to 8.7% and 2.8%, with reported EBITDA down more than two fifths to US$175m, or US$207m before severance [S2, p.48]. The net loss is much larger than the operating loss because US$21.0m of impaired receivables and US$11.4m of fixed-asset impairment sit below the operating line, outside the EBITDA we capitalise [S2, pp.35, 405].

Two restatements matter, and a third now applies to the earlier years. The pack's depreciation line is not the real charge: the notes show US$234.7m in FY2025 and US$255.4m in FY2024, split between cost of revenues and operating expenses, so a cash cost calibrated off the pack would be wrong by an order of magnitude [S2, p.362]. The same stub distorts the pack for FY2023 and FY2022; we restate both from the company's own EBITDA in the FY2024 report less the LK operating profit, which gives a monotonic history rather than the artefact in which EBITDA doubled in the year revenue fell [S10, p.14]. Finance cost was US$91.6m and US$102.7m against a blended balance above a billion dollars, a cash cost near nine per cent rather than the pack's lower figure, so we hold a blended cost of debt of 8.5% [S2, S6, pp.75, 80].

EBITDA is US$173.8m on the LK's own lines: the operating result of US$-68.0m [F43] plus total depreciation and amortisation of US$241.8m [F58], against the company's own US$175m measure [S2, pp.405-407]. The pack prints a lower operating result because it folds the Australian receivable provision into operating cost, which the LK does not. EBITDA is now the DCF's cash flow base and the screen's denominator, not a multiple metric; the ex-severance figure of US$207m [S2, p.48] is disclosed and not used.

Capital expenditure was US$177.6m in FY2025 and free cash flow to the firm US$62.8m, positive but small against the interest bill [S2]. In 1H2026 it generated US$63.8m of operating cash flow on US$692.8m of revenue, spent US$49.2m on fixed assets and reported EBITDA of US$69.0m, an improvement attributed to workforce optimisation and fuel efficiency but an efficiency story on a small base, not a spread recovery [S3, S6].

Net debt was US$872.7m at the year end, or 5.0 times our EBITDA and 5.1x on the company's, above the disclosed covenant level of three and a half times; waivers were obtained for the end-2025 and mid-2026 test dates; book equity fell from 51.6m to a few million dollars at the interim [S2, S6, p.77].

Our forecast holds the FY2025 cost structure in real terms. Revenue is -1.0% in FY2026E, then 2.5% from the named extensions; Adaro is a continuation, since the source says it "secures the continuation of BUMA's operations at South Tutupan" and quotes the volumes as the replacement term's gross, so we credit no incremental volume [S4]. The gross margin input is stated on a cash-cost basis, so that the depreciation the forecast adds back is the depreciation it deducts: 3.7% after the Brent link, against the 2.8% reported margin [S6, S2, p.362]. Capex is 7.5% of revenue in FY2026E rising to 10.2%, about seven tenths of depreciation: we assume the fleet is maintained rather than replaced, because the first half of FY2026 ran at US$49.2m of cash capex [S6, F35].

The margin step is disclosed rather than assumed, and it is no longer explained by a falling D&A ratio. EBITDA margin moves from 11.7% to 11.7%, reconciled in two sourced pieces: eight tenths from opex falling to six and a half per cent on the severance programme, and about a point against from the Brent fuel link (the deck's Brent path rising from about sixty-eight dollars to ninety-six, on a five per cent fuel share and half pass-through) [S6, S2]. A lower D&A charge is not a margin driver: D&A is added back in EBITDA and deducted again in EBIT, so it moves the split, not the total.

On those inputs EBITDA is US$170.9m and US$181.5m while finance cost rises above a hundred million dollars a year [S6]. Net income is US$-131.3m and US$-131.7m, and free cash flow to the firm is well below the interest bill, so equity cash flow is negative after the first year and the company rolls its maturities; debt rises from US$1,111.8m to US$1,478.8m by FY2030E and US$1,882.2m by FY2035E, and book equity becomes steadily more negative. We assume neither default nor a rescue issue, only refinancing at the current blended cost, the most likely path while the lenders are cooperative [S6]. The earnings-quality screens are unambiguous: accruals are heavy because depreciation exceeds EBITDA, the receivable provision shows revenue is not all collectable, and working capital has funded the business for two years [S2, S3].

The method set follows the business, not the industry code. DOID is listed in coal, but the fee business is the revenue, so a producer build would tie revenue to a Newcastle price and apply a royalty to service revenue; we use the corporate template and the contractor map, and the DCF carries the whole valuation [S2, p.60; S6, p.117]. The card this name is filed under is written for a producer — through-cycle price anchor, cost-curve quartile, reserve life, dividend-capacity yield against NAV — and DOID owns no reserve and sells no benchmark tonne, so the anchors are substituted rather than claimed: contract tenure and volume replace reserve life, the client's cost curve replaces our own AISC quartile, the fee per cubic metre replaces the realisation, and debt capacity replaces dividend capacity, because no distribution is payable while parent equity is negative [S2, S6]. That substitution is the reason the engine runs the corporate template, not the producer template.

The EV/EBITDA leg is retired at zero weight for a reason we can demonstrate rather than argue: on the data packs the engine prices, the trailing "EBITDA" field is an operating-profit field, because the pack's depreciation line is a stub [S0]. For DOID itself the pack's trailing figure sits within a few million dollars of the published operating profit while the LK charges US$241.8m of depreciation and amortisation [S2, F58]. A peer median built on that field is an EBIT median. P/E is unavailable: FY2025 was the second consecutive parent loss, with negative EPS [S2], so that leg contributes nothing and is recorded in dropped methods.

The cost of capital is built from a dollar risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and an Indonesia country premium of 2.5%, with an unlevered beta of 1.00 relevered at the engine's leverage cap of 2.00 times to 2.56: a cost of equity of 24.7% and, at a 33.3% equity weight, a WACC of 11.9% [S0]. The engine prices the debt leg at the macro spread of 7.0%, well below what DOID pays: bank facilities at six to seven and a quarter per cent and 2025 bonds up to eight and three quarters [F53], with a FY2025 finance cost of US$91.6m on opening debt near a billion dollars [S2, p.72; F9]. We therefore add a 2.6% premium to the cost of equity, lifting the WACC as repricing the debt at the blended 8.5% would, while the leverage cap flatters the equity [S6, pp.75, 80; F49, F50].

The discounted cash flow produces an enterprise value of US$306.5m. The terminal value is positive and 36.8% of that enterprise value: the forecast charges fleet replacement every year, and the terminal value is the continuing fee stream after the explicit horizon, not a liquidation. After the bridge the equity is negative, so limited liability floors the DCF value at zero. That is not an artefact: on our cash flows the enterprise is worth less than the debt, and the equity is a call option on the difference [S6].

The peer screen closes in the same direction as the DCF. The engine prices the packs' trailing "EBITDA" field, which is an operating-profit field; struck on it the peer median overstates the multiple, so the apparent cheapness of the peers is an artefact of a depreciation stub [S0]. Restruck on each peer's own LK depreciation the corrected median is lower, and at that lower multiple the implied enterprise value no longer covers the bridge from net debt to equity, so the screen corroborates the floor rather than adding value [S0, S2, p.362]. The packs are refreshed on different days within the month, so the set is not a synchronous snapshot and the screen is indicative rather than a point estimate [S0]. The leg therefore carries no weight, and the arithmetic of its retirement is written out in `fund record`, where it can be audited, rather than printed here as a number the engine does not compute.

The other half of the bridge is the associate book, and it is optionality rather than the floor. Both holdings stay at equity-method carrying value, US$123.4m at the interim date, of which the ASX-listed copper stake is the bulk [S6, p.4; F55]. The filings do give a dated mark: the 2026 top-up was AUD47.2m (US$33.1m) for 120.8m shares, and the group then held 395.6m shares at an effective 22.6% [S6, p.67; F56]. At that price the whole stake is worth less than its carrying value, so book is not conservative; marking it would trim the target by a few rupiah through the branch weight, not change the arithmetic of the branch. We keep book because it is the audited carrying value and a single 2026 purchase print is a transaction price, not a quoted market [S6]. The direction matters for the call: the bull equity is positive before the add-back, so a full write-off leaves the branch solvent and the target just above the price, turning BUY into HOLD. The add-back decides the rating, not the solvency, and the base and bear floor at zero with or without it [S0, F55].

The target of Rp187 is the probability-weighted scenario value after the 10.0% liquidity haircut [S0]. With the base branch at 60.0% floored at zero and the bear at 25.0% likewise, the whole of the weighted value comes from the bull at 15.0%, worth Rp1,382 per share [S0]. Within the branch, the two mirrored operating shocks alone do not clear the debt: the engine's revenue-and-margin grid is at the floor in every cell but the most extreme, and that cell is worth a fraction of the bull's value. The equity is produced by the capex ratio, at a fifth below the normalised 10.2%. That is the driver the price is really being asked to believe, and it is sourced to the ratios the company has actually run [S2, p.72; S6, p.10].

The weight is the input to test, and it has a basis rather than a preference. The house base-rate library's commodity-capex-turnaround archetype is a three-year prior; annualised to the twelve-month branch it implies a hit rate in the teens, and we hold 15.0% just below it, because a contractor with covenants waived is more fragile than the producer sample the prior is drawn from [S0, S6, p.77]. The price implies a lower weight still: the target equals the current price at a bull weight of a little below eleven per cent, roughly four points under ours, so the entire expected return is the gap between the two readings. The exact figures are in `fund record`, where they can be audited against the engine [S0].

The price is not valuing the base case either. At Rp133 the equity is worth a small fraction of net debt, which is what a call option on the enterprise looks like: the market is paying for a recovery branch, not for today's cash flows [S0, S6]. Where we differ from the price is in the probability that branch arrives and in what it is worth if it does. A reverse DCF cannot be computed here, because the base value is floored at zero across the plausible range of discount rates and growth, so there is no implied price to solve for. Two house screens fail and the reader should see them: the investability test passes board quality but fails on market capitalisation and on liquidity, with three-month ADTV of IDR1.1bn, and the 10.0% discount in the target is the standard charge for that illiquidity [S0]. A BUY below the house size threshold is a size-constrained position, not a core holding.

The first sensitivity grid varies cost of capital and terminal growth and every cell is zero: enterprise value stays below net debt across a plausible band, so limited liability holds the equity at the floor [S0]. The second varies revenue growth and gross margin and stays at the floor until the margin recovery is large enough for the unlevered value to clear net debt; past that point it moves sharply, because every dollar of enterprise value above the debt accrues to an equity that has been priced near zero. That leverage cuts both ways, which is why the bull's capex ratio — not the margin cell — is the variable that decides the rating; the two operating shocks alone are inside this grid and do not clear the debt. A return to the FY2024 gross margin of 8.7% would clear it on that branch alone, but the base is anchored to the last actual, 2.8%, so that recovery belongs in the bull [S2, S6].

The dominant risk is refinancing: equity cash flow is negative, so the company rolls maturities every year, and it has already needed covenant waivers for the last two test dates [S6, p.77; F29]. The syndicated facility matures in 2029 [S6, p.75; F51], Muamalat in 2028 [F52], and the sukuk and bonds total US$185.0m gross, of which US$39.3m is current [S6, pp.69, 75, 81]. The next test is 31 December 2026. If the lenders tighten, the equity is diluted or extinguished before the operating story improves. No default branch is modelled, so the bear is the recession that would precede one and default is a tail beyond the table, which makes the target, if anything, high rather than low. Mapping likelihood to impact: refinancing is likely and existential; the loss of a contract is unlikely and material; fuel and currency are likely and modest; a governance shock is unlikely and impairing, because it would arrive through the same lender channel.

The recapitalisation branch is the one the table cannot express. Net debt is US$872.7m against an equity the market prices at a fraction of it, free cash flow to the firm does not cover the interest bill, and the covenants have been waived rather than met [S6; F29]. We do not forecast a debt-for-equity conversion: no such agreement is disclosed, and the waiver is the company's answer so far. But if one comes it transfers value from existing shares to lenders, because converting anything like the debt at today's price would issue a multiple of the existing share count; we therefore treat it as dilution to zero recovery rather than as a rescue. No rights issue is modelled either: one sized to a year of the shortfall would materially increase the share count and no controlling-shareholder commitment exists [S6].

The operating risks are second-layer, and their tenures are not equal. The top five customers are 78.0% of revenue [F26]; Indonesia Pratama, the largest of them, is contracted to August 2035 [S10, p.123; F63], beyond the horizon, while the Adaro South Tutupan award runs only to the end of 2030 [S4; F27, F28]. The dated cliff is therefore the smaller exposure and the largest relationship is not the one to fear, which is why no branch assumes Pratama away. Fuel pass-through is lagged [S3, S6]; weather reduced FY2024 volumes [S5]; and a weaker rupiah helps the translated target while hurting dollar costs [S0]. The upside is narrower: a sustained fall in Brent would restore margin, and a new award would add volume without proportional capital. The associate is not clean upside either: the add-back is what lifts the bull target from HOLD to BUY, and a mark-down removes that lift, though it does not make the branch insolvent [S6, p.4; F55].

Scenarios are mirrored on revenue growth, gross margin and capital intensity, and read as two states of the capital structure rather than three forecasts of the coal cycle. In the bear, clients cut stripping plans, the Adaro award is not renewed beyond its dated expiry and the cost programme stalls: revenue declines against the base's rise, margin gives back the recovery, capex runs above the base ratio and the lenders roll the facility only at a higher margin [S6]. The revenue shock is the mirror of the bull's increase and is sized to the one dated expiry inside the forecast; the largest contract, Pratama to 2035, is not assumed lost in any branch, because nothing in the record says it is at risk [S10, p.123; F63]. The engine floors the DCF at zero in both the bear and the base, so the two rows carry the same value: the difference between them is real, but the equity cannot show it. The base carries 60.0% of the mass, the bear 25.0% and the bull 15.0%.

In the bull the Adaro rollover and the cost programme hold, new awards extend the contract base, Brent falls along the deck and capex runs a fifth below our base ratio of 10.2%, which puts it between the 7.2% spent in FY2023 and the 10.0% in FY2024, and below the 12.0% of FY2025 [S0, S2, p.72], while still above the US$49.2m spent in 1H2026 [S6, p.10; F35]. That ratio, not the margin, is what clears net debt in the branch: the operating improvement alone leaves the shares worth a fraction of the price, because the equity is a thin sliver on a US$872.7m debt stack, so small changes in terminal capital intensity move the value by an order of magnitude. The associate book of US$123.4m is what lifts the target from HOLD to BUY, a lift of about a quarter of the target; a full write-off would leave the branch's own value intact and the weighted target just above the price, so the stake is a rating risk rather than a solvency one, and the associates' negative share of profit in the half year [S6, p.67] is why we mark it at book rather than above it. The weighted value is Rp207 per share and Rp187 after the haircut; the base-case value is Rp0, also below the price. The gap to the band above is the weight on the bull branch.

The signposts are the covenant test dates, the quarterly cash-flow statement, net debt and headroom, overburden volume since the monthly production report was discontinued [S5], and any announcement on the maturity profile or a capital raise. A refinancing that extends maturities without adding debt would remove the binary risk and change the rating without an operating improvement [S6].

Northstar Tambang Persada controls 38.2% of the shares, with Six Sis and Trimegah Sekuritas also above the reporting threshold; the free float is 45.5% and treasury shares remain from the buyback [S2, p.88; S0]. The auditor is KAP Aria Kanaka & Rekan, a Forvis Mazars member, with an unmodified opinion; interims are unaudited but reviewed, covenant waivers sit in the notes and related-party transactions are not material [S2; S6, p.77].

The dividend record is the clearest governance signal: the last distribution was the final dividend for FY2023, none has been paid for FY2024 or FY2025, and there is no capacity while net debt is above five times EBITDA, covenants are waived and parent equity is negative [S2, p.152; F34; S6]; we model none through FY2030E. On ESG the exposure is contract mining's footprint: safety, dust and emissions from a diesel fleet, land rehabilitation and community relations [S2]. The energy transition is a structural negative for thermal volumes, partly offset by metallurgical and copper exposure. It is neither a konglo name nor an index-deletion candidate.

The dated catalysts are the quarterly and half-year reports, each carrying a covenant test, and the full-year results in the first quarter of FY2027 [S6]. The Adaro ramp and 2030 expiry are the main operating catalysts; any refinancing statement addresses the binary risk [S4, S6]. We monitor overburden volume, gross margin, operating cash flow against capex, net debt, Brent and the rupiah; the monthly production report was discontinued after December 2024, leaving the quarterly disclosure as the only operating data point [S5].

S0.title: Yahoo Finance statements, prices and profile for DOID.JK

S4.title: Detik: BUMA extends Adaro contract 44 Mt

S6.title: BUMA interim consolidated financial statements 30 June 2026

S9.title: Warta Ekonomi: ESDM evaluates DMO, 2026 coal output 720 Mt

bear.narrative: Coal clients cut RKAB volumes and the Adaro book at South Tutupan — 13% of revenue, contracted to 31 December 2030 [S6 p.106, S4] — is not renewed, so revenue falls a further two points a year on top of the four-point operating decline (a loss of about 13% by FY2035, matching the dated Adaro share), fuel and wage costs take two points of gross margin and capex rises a fifth as the smaller volume is spread over a fixed fleet; the x1.2 capex shock puts the ratio at 12.2% of revenue, sized to the 12.0% the company actually spent in FY2025 [F18, S2 p.72]. PT Indonesia Pratama, 35% of revenue and contracted to August 2035 [S6 p.123], is NOT assumed lost: no source puts its term inside the forecast, so the bear takes the disclosed expiry only. Free cash flow does not cover interest [S6], the lenders roll the syndicated facility that matures 69 months after first utilisation [F51] only at a higher margin, and the 31 December 2026 covenant test [S6 p.77] is the point at which a debt-for-equity conversion becomes the recovery route for the lenders. Equity recovery in that branch is zero, which is why the row is valued at the DCF floor; a negative equity value is not available under limited liability. A further mark-down of the US$123.4m associate book [F55] would take that branch's investment add-back to zero too, but the branch is already worth nothing to equity holders, so it adds no separate sensitivity here.

bull.narrative: The branch is a capital-intensity case, not a margin story, and the decomposition is written out here so the report and the engine say the same thing. On the base case the DCF enterprise value is US$306.5m against an US$887.1m bridge, so the equity is floored at zero. The two mirrored operating shocks alone - revenue +4pp a year and gross margin +2pp - raise the twelve-month value only to Rp57.0 (v0 Rp45.7), still effectively floored because the margin recovery is not large enough to cover the debt. The branch clears the debt on capex: a fifth below the base's normalised 10.2% puts the ratio at 8.2% of revenue from FY2027E, between the 7.2% actually spent in FY2023 and the 10.0% in FY2024 and below FY2025's 12.0% [F18, S2 p.72]; FY2026E is leaner still (6.0%) on the branch assumption that the 1H2026 deferral (US$49.2m of fixed-asset spend) extends [F35, S6 p.10]. The capex shock contributes US$429m of the branch's US$447.3m equity (Rp1,063 of the Rp1,109 per-share value): the branch clears the debt on the capex ratio, not on the margin recovery. What is underwritten is the contracted book - PT Indonesia Pratama at 35% of revenue to August 2035, an eleven-year extension the company put at US$7.8bn in contract value [S6 p.123, F63, S5], the Adaro rollover at South Tutupan [S4, F27, F28], and the US$12.7bn order book published with the FY2025 results [F38, S5] - and the 1H2026 cost programme. The equity is positive BEFORE the associate stake is added: ex-associate the branch is worth Rp803 per share and the weighted target Rp135, above the Rp133 price but HOLD rather than BUY. The associate book (US$123.4m at equity-method carrying value, F55) therefore lifts the target from HOLD to BUY [S6 p.4]; it is not what makes the branch solvent, and a full write-off does not floor it. The bear's mirrored capex shock is x1.2, i.e. 12.2% of revenue, sized to the 12.0% the company actually spent in FY2025 [F18, S2 p.72].

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: 1H2026 revenue was US$692.8m, 5.1% below 1H2025's US$730.2m [F20, F22, S6], and LTM revenue is US$1,442.9m (data pack), so FY2026E is set at -1.0%. The Adaro contract signed on 23 February 2026 and running 1 April 2026-31 December 2030 is a CONTINUATION, not an addition: the source says it "mengamankan keberlanjutan operasional BUMA di Tambang Tutupan Selatan" - it secures the continuation of BUMA's operations at South Tutupan in a relationship of more than twenty years - and the 239 million bcm and 44 Mt it quotes (50.5 million bcm and 9.3 Mt a year) are the gross volumes of a replacement contract, whose first day follows the expiry of the previous Adaro term [F27, F28, S4]. We therefore model no incremental volume from it, and the prior contract's exact expiry date is not disclosed in the archive, which is why the assumption takes the conservative reading rather than claiming a ramp. FY2027E +2.5% comes from the named extensions only - Blackwater (to June 2030), Goonyella Riverside (to September 2027) and Whitehaven [S2, p.49] - and is not the first full year of a new Adaro book. FY2028E-FY2030E step down to +2.0%, +1.5% and +1.5%. We do not translate the US$12.7bn order book [F38, S5] into a growth rate: it is total contract value over multi-year terms (about 8.6x FY2025 revenue), while annual revenue is set by each client's yearly mine plan, and the awards disclosed since it was published are already in the forecast. The deceleration is therefore contract arithmetic on the disclosed terms, not a statement that the backlog has run off. No formal volume or revenue guidance is published. LT 2.0% is the macro deck's long-run USD inflation, not real growth.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Stated AFTER the depreciation carried in cost of revenues, the way the LK prints it, but rebased so that no D&A is deducted twice. FY2025 reported gross margin was 2.81% (revenue US$1,480.3m, COGS US$1,438.7m) [F1, F3, S2] and that margin already carries the D&A charged to profit or loss, 16.33% of revenue (US$241.8m [F58, S2 p.362]). The forecast adds back only the 14.5% da_pct [S6], so holding the reported 2.81% would deduct 1.83 points of D&A the forecast never charges and understate EBITDA by roughly US$27m a year - the double-count the review identified. Cash COGS is the invariant: 2.81% + 16.33% = 19.14% of revenue before D&A, so at 14.5% D&A the reported gross margin input is 4.64%. 1H2026 was 1.76% reported, 14.2% on the same cash basis (COGS US$680.7m including US$96.8m of depreciation) [F20, S6 p.107], which is the fuel squeeze the Brent link below carries, not a structural step, so the input stays at the FY2025 cash level and the link does the work. Costs otherwise stay at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Fuel is a direct cost line of US$153.4m in 1H2026, 22.5% of the US$680.7m cost of revenues [S6, p.107], but only part of it moves with Brent: the fuel line rose 14% year on year into 1H2026 while the deck's Brent rose from 68.1 to 96.0 (+41%), because Indonesian HSD is administered and lagged and volumes fell. The observed cost effect is what calibrates the share: gross margin fell from 2.81% in FY2025 to 1.75% in 1H2026, about one point, for a Brent move of roughly two fifths [F1, F3, F20, S6]. With half of that passed into rates, the COGS share that behaves like Brent is about 5%, not the full 22.5% fuel line, which would overstate the cost swing in both directions.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: The fuel line in cost of revenues rose to US$153.4m in 1H2026 from US$134.4m in 1H2025, a US$19.1m increase [F47, F48, S6 p.107]. The company states that excluding that fuel-price increase 1H2026 EBITDA would have been close to US$78m against US$69m reported [F21, S3], i.e. about US$9m of the US$19.1m increase was absorbed and roughly half was recovered in service rates within the year. The balance sits in the margin until the next contract reset; we hold 50% pass-through for the forecast.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses were US$108.7m, 7.34% of revenue [F5, F1, S2]; 1H2026 was US$44.9m, 6.48% of revenue [S6, p.7]. We hold the nine-month run-rate at 6.5% rather than the FY2025 ratio, because the FY2025 number carried severance and impairment-related charges that the company identifies as one-off (EBITDA ex-severance US$207m) [F31, S2]. No cost-cut is assumed beyond the observed level.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A charged to profit or loss was US$234.7m (US$231.9m in COGS and US$2.8m in opex) [F7, S2 p.362], 15.9% of revenue; FY2024 was US$255.4m [F8]. 1H2026 depreciation fell with the asset base after disposals and impairments (US$96.8m in COGS plus US$1.3m in opex and US$1.4m amortisation), about 14.4% of revenue [S6, pp.63,107]. We hold 14.5% for the forecast, below FY2025 because the fleet base is smaller, and never calibrate a cash cost off the Yahoo D&A line, which is a fraction of the real charge.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross capex was US$177.6m (12.0% of revenue), including US$169.5m of fixed assets [F18, S2 p.72], US$6.4m of mining properties and US$1.7m of intangibles; FY2024 was US$175.5m (10.0%) on a D&A charge of US$255.4m [F8, F19], and FY2023 was US$131.8m (7.2%). Capex has therefore run at 69% of D&A in FY2024 (175.5/255.4) and 73% in FY2025 (177.6/241.8 of total depreciation and amortisation), not at the 58.6% the previous version of this file implied: 8.5% of revenue is not seventy per cent of a 14.5% D&A charge, 10.15% is. We start FY2026E at 7.5%, close to the 1H2026 fixed-asset run-rate of 7.1% of revenue [F35, S6 p.10], then normalise to 10.2%, which is seventy per cent of the 14.5% D&A rate and US$150-160m a year against the FY2025 actual of US$177.6m for the same fleet. Holding capex at 8.5% would have understated the cash cost of the fleet by about US$24m a year and flattered free cash flow.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 net working capital was US$77.8m on revenue of US$1,480.3m, 5.3%; 1H2026 was US$65.8m on US$692.8m, 9.5% on a seasonal low revenue base [S0, S6]. We hold 6.0% of revenue, close to the FY2025 level and above the FY2024 7.6% peak, with no unsourced working-capital release.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Zero cash tax in the forecast, not the 22% statutory rate: the group is loss-making every year to 2035E on these inputs (PBT negative from FY2024), so there is no tax to pay and no tax credit to book. Applying 22% to a negative EBIT would create a phantom 15m-a-year credit in the engine's FCFF line; the statutory rate only becomes relevant if the profit path turns, which the base case does not assume. Accumulated tax losses are not capitalised as an asset.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance cost was US$91.6m on opening debt of US$1,002.7m (9.1%); FY2024 was US$102.7m on US$1,190.7m (8.6%) [F9, F10, S2]. The bank facilities carried 7.64%-8.39% at 30 June 2026 [S6, p.80] and the Senior Notes and leases sit above that, so 8.5% is the blended run-rate, not the Yahoo 7.49%.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income was US$4.1m on opening cash of US$211.4m, 1.9% [S0, S2]; 1H2026 interest received was US$1.8m. We hold 2.0%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: 1H2026 was a net repayment year: US$57.5m of bank draws against US$52.3m bank repayments, US$31.9m of Senior Notes repaid, US$12.9m of long-term debt and US$21.8m of leases, a net outflow of about US$61m [S6, p.10]. That repayment was funded from a cash balance of US$211.4m at the start of the year, which fell to US$158.5m by 30 June 2026 [S6]. Repeating it is not available: on the forecast the annual interest bill of roughly US$90m exceeds FCFF of US$24-29m, so free cash flow to equity is negative and the company must refinance rather than deleverage. We therefore model net new borrowing of about US$70-75m a year, which holds cash near the 30 June 2026 level and rolls the shortfall, with debt roughly flat in nominal terms. This is a refinancing treadmill, not growth capex and not a deleveraging assumption; it is why the equity is a thin option on enterprise value.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2025 other income of US$58.3m and other expenses of US$57.5m net to US$0.8m [S2, p.68]; we hold zero and do not capitalise the 1H2026 land-sale gain or FX gains, which the company itself labels non-operational [S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interest on the balance sheet was negative US$1.9m at 30 June 2026 [S0, S6] and the minority share of FY2025 losses was US$11.3m on a US$127.6m group loss; the minority positions are immaterial and loss-making, so we model zero attribution rather than the pack's average ratio distorted by negative profit.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend was paid for FY2024 or FY2025; the last was US$10m for FY2023 (US$5m interim and US$5m final paid July 2024) [F34, S2 p.152]. With net debt/EBITDA at 5.10x, covenants waived at 30 June 2026 [F30, F29] and negative parent equity, no distribution is assumed through the forecast. Any dividend is an upside, not a base-case cash flow.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares outstanding were 7,357,169,432 after 293,837,700 treasury shares at 31 December 2025 [F11, S2]; the 2025 buyback was completed, and no rights issue or placement is announced. We hold the count flat and do not assume a rescue equity raise, which would be a scenario, not the base case.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: USD reporting currency: 2.0% is the macro deck's long-run US inflation anchor (Federal Reserve 2 percent goal), not real growth. A contractor with no perpetual reserve should not grow faster than the currency it bills in over the long run.

challenges.challenge: The multiple the entire target rests on is not an EBITDA multiple. fund record lines 816-845 compute each peer's EV/EBITDA from datapack ltm.ebitda; in DOID's own pack that field is -82.52 for FY2025A and -51.15 LTM with da of 5.57, against the LK's USD175m (S2 p.48) and the model's 173.81 - i.e. it is EBIT (1,480.3 - 1,438.7 - 129.7 = -88.1, the 129.7 being the pack's opex including the provision). Peers have the same shape: ADMR da 0.816 on revenue 972.9, BYAN 1.972 on 3,427.6, PTBA 300 IDR bn on 42,652. A 5.142591x multiple struck on an EBIT-like base and applied to DOID's true EBITDA of 173.81 overstates EV by 5.14 x 241.8 = ~USD1.24bn; on a like-for-like EBIT base DOID's -68 gives a negative cross-check. The report asserts the peer denominators are reported trailing EBITDA but cites no peer LK.
challenges.answer: Confirmed on every peer pack: ltm.ebitda is an EBIT field because the pack da line is a stub (ADMR 559.2 vs EBIT 558.2 with D&A 44.0; BYAN 1,091.7 vs 1,089.7 with 111.1; DOID -51.1 vs -56.8 with LK D&A 234.7) [S0, S2 p.362]. Rebuilt on the 17 peers with LK-sourced FY2025 depreciation the median is 3.75x, not 5.15x; at 3.75x EV is US$651.8m against a US$761.8m bridge, so equity is negative and the leg floors at zero. Retired at weight 0.00; multiple_basis rewritten and section 4 shows the leg only as a floored screen line.

challenges.challenge: The distance from the REDUCE line is misstated sixfold. Solving the model's own arithmetic (v0 58.9343 = 0.18 x 327.413; V = 430.99 x m - 1,888.02; target = 0.20207 x V + 18.60) gives m = 5.2705, i.e. +2.49% on 5.142591, to reach Rp96 (three quarters of Rp128; sell_max_pct -25.0, fund rules 309). A median about a seventh higher (5.877) prices Rp148.8, BUY territory. So SELL is 2.5% of peer-median noise from REDUCE - smaller than the 2.24% refresh the report says produced the move - and the packs are refreshed on different days (KKGI/ARII 2026-11-12 04:12, ADMR/BSSR 11 Nov, INDY 7 Nov, MYOH 6 Nov), so that noise is live.
challenges.answer: Accepted: with the multiple leg retired there is no peer-median distance to a REDUCE line, so the Rp96 at 5.27x and Rp149 at 5.88x arithmetic is withdrawn rather than restated. Weight is 1.00 DCF plus the retired floor, and the sentence claiming the old target was 'no longer a boundary case' is deleted. The boundary the report now describes is the one the engine computes [S0].

challenges.challenge: The DCF is nominally primary at 82% and contributes exactly zero everywhere: fund record valuation.scenarios base and bear are both v0 58.9343 / tp 73.5114, and sensitivities[1].grid is 73.511368 in all 25 cells. The published target is therefore 100% (0.18 x one cross-check), and 93.4% of that cross-check's equity value (USD123.4 of USD132.1) is the 29Metals associate at equity-method book. At the industry-default 25% multiple weight the target is Rp109 (REDUCE); at the prior 15% it is Rp74.5. The 18% is a payoff correction (15% x 1.17) dressed as a confidence weight.
challenges.answer: Accepted in substance. The target is no longer weight x multiple: weight is 100% DCF, base and bear floor at zero, and the associate is disclosed at equity-method book US$123.4m [S6 p.4, F55]. No ASX price for the 22.6% copper stake is in the archive, and section 4 says so rather than implying a mark; the add-back no longer carries the target [S6 p.67, F56, F57].

challenges.challenge: D&A is double-deducted. gross_margin is held at FY2025's 2.81%, struck after D&A of USD241.8m = 16.33% of revenue (F58), while da_pct is 14.5%; the engine adds back only revenue x 14.5% (fund record lines.da), so ~1.8pp (~USD27m) of D&A no longer in the cost base is deducted, partly offset by the opex cut to 6.5% - net EBITDA understated by about USD15m (10%), and the calibration gate reads 9.80% against an 11.74% actual. Section 3's reconciliation (one and four-fifths from the D&A ratio falling) treats a lower D&A charge as an EBITDA cost, which is backwards.
challenges.answer: Accepted and fixed. gross_margin is now 4.64%, holding cash COGS constant at FY2025's 19.14% of revenue before D&A (2.81% reported + 16.33% D&A - 14.5% da_pct) [S2, F1, F3, F58]. The calibration gate reads actual 11.74% against model 11.66%, and the D&A-ratio sentence is removed from section 3. The DCF still floors.

challenges.challenge: The scenario table is not a distribution: bear and base carry the same value (both floored DCF plus static multiple, tp 73.51), so the 25% bear adds nothing and doubling it leaves the target unchanged - only the 15% bull moves the number. The one-sided -6pp revenue-growth shock compounds to about -47% of revenue by FY2035, while the only quantified client exposure (Adaro, 50.5 mbcm and 9.3 Mt a year, S4) is ~11% of FY2025 volume (439 mbcm / 84 Mt, S2) and the largest customer, PT Indonesia Pratama, is 35% of revenue (S6 p.106) with no disclosed term.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The -6pp compounding shock is deleted. The bear's second revenue shock is -2pp, sized to the one dated expiry inside the forecast, Adaro at 13% to 31 Dec 2030 [S6 p.106, S4, F27, F28], and compounds to about that share. The bear narrative now names recap-at-zero and the 31 Dec 2026 covenant test as the recovery route [S6 p.77], and Pratama's term to Aug 2035 is disclosed [S10 p.123, F63].

challenges.challenge: The bull only mirrors the three shocks and omits documented upside: the USD12.7bn order book (F38, S5) is in fund record and never used; 1H2026 free cash flow was +USD39m (S3) with capex at 7.1% of revenue (F35) against the base's 10.2%; the associate is held at book with no market check although copper rose (S2 p.32). The bull's DCF equity sits within roughly 8% of net debt and is highly geared, so any of these could change the bull materially.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part. The bull now cites the US$12.7bn order book and its date [F38, S5] and the Pratama extension to 2035 [S5, F63]. Capex is set at 8.2% of revenue rather than the 7.1% 1H2026 run-rate, because a half-year spend is deferral not steady state and the fleet cannot be run down while revenue grows; that is stated and sourced in the bull narrative [S6 p.10, F35]. The associate has no ASX price in the archive and stays at book.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 calls a debt-for-equity conversion the modal outcome, yet 60% of the mass sits on refinancing at the current blended cost with equity worth Rp74, and no branch prices a zero. If the text is right (>50% recap) the target is too high; if the weights are right the modal claim is unsourced. The bear also omits the associate risk (a USD14.5m fair-value loss already in 1H2026, post_bs_review) and the 31 December 2026 covenant test after waivers for both prior dates (S6 p.77).
challenges.answer: Accepted. The unsourced 'modal outcome' claim is removed. The bear narrative now states that the 31 Dec 2026 covenant test [S6 p.77] is where a debt-for-equity conversion becomes the lenders' recovery route and that equity recovery is zero, so the branch is carried at the floor; a separate recap branch would carry the same zero value. The associate write-down sensitivity is added in section 5 [S6 p.67, F55].

challenges.challenge: Weights are typed dcf 0.82 / ev 0.18 / pe 0.15, summing to 1.15, while weights_basis says the pair sums to one. It is inert only because P/E is dropped; if EPS ever turns positive the engine renormalises all three, the multiple leg falls to ~15.7% and the target moves to about Rp74 with no operating change.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The weights are dcf_fcff 1.0, ev_ebitda 0.0 and pe 0.0, summing to exactly 1.00, so no renormalisation can restore the multiple leg if EPS turns positive [S0].

challenges.challenge: The 'What changed' paragraph attributes the whole 97-to-85 and REDUCE-to-SELL move to the peer refresh, but the repository shows otherwise. At 6e523b65^ the engine already printed tp_final Rp93.59, tr -26.88% and rating SELL on multiple 5.259107x and fx 18,103 (fund rules sell_max_pct -25.0); 6e523b65 moved the multiple to 5.142591x and tp to Rp84.86 at an unchanged Rp128; the only working-tree change since is the price 128 to 133. The 97 came from v3's hand-built target ('reverting to the branch weight alone gives about ninety-six rupiah ... still REDUCE', v3 section 4), 3.6% above its own model. So 97-to-93.59 is a report/model gap being closed, not a peer refresh, and the engine has never rated this name REDUCE at 5.259x.
challenges.answer: Accepted: the 97 was not an engine output. The prior engine run printed tp_final Rp93.59, tr -26.88% and rating SELL on multiple 5.259107x at fx 18,103; the refresh took the multiple to 5.142591x at fx 18,240 and the only working-tree change was the price 128 to 133. v3's Rp97 was a hand target to the branch weight. The Investment summary now states that decomposition [S0].

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis, table:fin_summary and fund record lines.da
challenges.challenge: The five-year EBITDA history is wrong before FY2024. fund record lines.da is 4.10 for FY2022A and 4.43 for FY2023A (pack:da, the same stub that prints 5.57 for FY2025A against the LK's 234.7 [F7]), then 261.22 and 241.81 for FY2024A/25A only because F8/F7 overrode it: a 59x step in one year. Since EBITDA = ebit + da, the summary carries US$135.4m (FY2022A) and US$151.2m (FY2023A) against US$314.2m (FY2024A), i.e. EBITDA doubling in the year revenue fell 4.2%, which contradicts the section's own 'reported EBITDA down more than two fifths' measured from FY2024.
challenges.answer: Accepted. FY2022A and FY2023A D&A are restated from the company's own annual report: reported EBITDA US$365m less operating profit US$131.3m, and US$412m less US$146.8m, added as F61 and F62 [S10 p.14]. lines.da now reads 233.7 / 265.2 / 261.2 / 241.8 and EBITDA 365.0 / 412.0 / 314.2 / 173.8, monotonic with the text of section 3.

challenges.challenge: The paragraph documenting the only positive valuation input describes a different run from the one that produced the target. It states the peer median is 5.26x at Rp18,103, bracketed by ARII 5.19x and INDY 5.33x, mean 7.82x and restruck 5.25x; fund record valuation.methods.ev_ebitda.multiple is 5.142591 at market.fx 18,240, and model.peers gives median 5.142591, mean 7.205, brackets KKGI 5.137 and ARII 5.148 (INDY 5.312). The 2.2% gap between 5.26 and 5.14 is the same size as the move the report attributes to the refresh, and the claim that Rp18,103 is 'the rate the engine reads from the pack' is false (18,240).
challenges.answer: Accepted. multiple_basis is rewritten to the live rebuild rather than the pre-refresh snapshot: the peer median is 3.75x on the 2026-11-11/12 packs, superseding 5.26x at 18,103, and the FX sentence is corrected to 18,240 [S0]. The stale figures are labelled superseded rather than printed as current.

challenges.challenge: The one-sided -6pp-a-year contract-loss shock is not sized to the disclosed contract terms. The largest customer, PT Indonesia Pratama at 35% of 1H2026 revenue [S6 p.106], is contracted May 2018 to August 2035 [S6 p.123, mining-services contract table]; Adaro is 13% of revenue and runs to 31 December 2030 [S6 p.106, S4]; TEC Coal is 13% and Whitehaven 10%. The only expiry inside the forecast is therefore Adaro at 13%, while the bear compounds to roughly -47% of revenue, and the review record's earlier statement that Pratama's term is undisclosed is wrong.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear is sized to the disclosed expiries: Adaro 13% from 31 Dec 2030 [S6 p.106, S4, F27, F28], with Pratama at 35% contracted to Aug 2035 and expressly not lost [S10 p.123, F63]; the shock compounds to about the Adaro share, not -47%. The bull now recognises the eleven-year extension and the US$7.8bn contract value [S5].

challenges.challenge: At the refreshed Rp133 price the SELL/REDUCE line is Rp99.75, not the Rp96 implied by the old Rp128. The target is 0.20207 x (448.91m - 1,888.5) = 90.71m - 381.6, so REDUCE needs m = 5.307x, i.e. +3.2% on 5.142591, not 'a peer median about a seventh higher' (+14.3%, which prices about Rp152, +14%, in the ADD band). The report understates the distance to the boundary by about 4.5x; C2's Rp96 / 5.27x / +2.5% figures were struck at Rp128 and are superseded by these.
challenges.answer: Accepted and superseded: the 'a seventh higher' sentence is deleted together with the multiple leg, so no peer-median boundary is printed. Section 4 now states that the peer packs are refreshed on different days within the month and that the screen is indicative rather than a point estimate [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: C6 stands; add the 11-year PT Indonesia Pratama extension (USD7.8bn, S5) and its contract term to August 2035 (S6 p.123), which underwrite 35% of revenue through the forecast and are not used anywhere; the 22.6% ASX-listed 29Metals stake (USD123.4m book = 93.4% of the cross-check's equity) is still unmarked although a market price exists.

missing_bear_case.note: C7 stands on direction but not on its Pratama claim: S6 p.123 shows the 35% customer contracted May 2018-August 2035, so the earlier note that its term is undisclosed is corrected here. The 31 December 2026 covenant test after waivers for both earlier dates (S6 p.77), an associate write-down (a USD14.5m fair-value loss is already in 1H2026) and a zero-recovery branch are still absent.

assumption_realism.note: The D&A double-count in C4 is real and larger than stated: gross margin is held at FY2025's 2.81%, struck after USD241.8m of D&A [F58], while the engine adds back only revenue x 14.5%, so ~1.94pp of revenue (~USD28m, 18% of FY2026E EBITDA) is deducted twice; the opex cut to 6.5% from 7.34% is sourced. FY2022A/23A D&A is the pack stub (C10), and the 2.5% FY2027E growth is sourced to the named Blackwater/Goonyella/Whitehaven extensions (S2 p.49).

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified in the archive: F26 78% top-five and Pratama 35% (S6 p.106); F27/F28 239 mbcm/44 Mt and 50.5/9.3 a year (S4); F31/F42 207/175 (S2 p.48, whose '44% margin' line is garbled but the dollars match); F53 6.75/8.00/8.75% (S6 p.71); F21/F60 69/64 (S3); 1H2026 equity USD4.4m; Blackwater to Jun 2030 and Goonyella to Sep 2027 (S2 p.49); Pratama to Aug 2035 (S6 p.123). Failures: multiple_basis is stale (C11), FY2022-23 history is wrong (C10), the 97/REDUCE provenance is unexplained (C9). No consensus contamination and the report is placeholder-based (43 placeholders).

findings.finding: The 15% bull weight basis is the house library archetype commodity_capex_turnaround (rate 0.42 over 3 years, n=40, annualised 16.6%), documented in fund record but cited in the report and the probability_basis as [S0] (Yahoo Finance data). The substance verifies; the citation label does not point at the document that holds the prior.

The prior is borrowed from a producer archetype whose payoff is +75%/-35% over three years, while the bull branch pays about +940%; probability and payoff therefore come from different distributions. The report argues the level (15% versus 16.6%) but not the reference-class transfer from producer to levered fee contractor.

The base and bear branches are valued at the limited-liability floor of zero in the twelve-month target, so 85% of the mass is priced as worthless even though neither branch assumes default and the market pays Rp133 today. The direction is conservative (the weighted target understates an option-value treatment of the floored states) and the floor is disclosed, but the report does not say that this biases the expected return downward.

flags.message: a.revenue_growth: bear -0.02 vs bull 0.04 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear's second revenue shock is -2pp a year, not the -6pp of the previous version: it is sized to the one dated expiry inside the forecast, Adaro at 13% of revenue to 31 December 2030 [S6 p.106, S4], and compounds to roughly that 13% loss by FY2035. The largest customer, PT Indonesia Pratama at 35% of revenue, is contracted to August 2035 [S6 p.123] and is not lost in the bear. The asymmetry against the bull's +4pp remains because a dated loss is disclosed while no award of that size is dated on the upside; mirroring it would require an unsourced new contract [S6 p.106, S4]. The other two drivers are exactly mirrored: gross margin +2pp / -2pp, and capex x0.8 / x1.2, with the bull at 8.2% of revenue between the 7.2% and 10.0% actually spent in FY2023-24 [F18, S2 p.72] and the bear at 12.2%, sized to the 12.0% actually spent in FY2025 [F18, S2 p.72]. The symmetry flag is on revenue growth only.

flags.message: expected return +40%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The +40% expected return is the bull branch probability-weighted against a floored base, and its drivers are named, sourced and sized in the branch: (1) capex at 8.2% of revenue from FY2027E, between the 7.2% spent in FY2023 and the 10.0% in FY2024 and below FY2025's 12.0% [F18, S2 p.72], with 1H2026 at 7.1% [F35, S6 p.10]; (2) revenue +4pp a year on the contracted book - Pratama at 35% of revenue to August 2035 [S6 p.123, F63] and Adaro to 2030 [S4]; (3) gross margin +2pp, still below the cash margins the company printed in FY2024 and FY2023 [S2, S10]. The engine's decomposition is the honest reading: the two operating shocks alone print tp Rp57.0, and the full branch prints Rp1,383, so the branch clears the US$887.1m net-debt bridge on the capex ratio, not on the margin recovery; the capex shock contributes US$429m of the US$447.3m equity. The equity is about two fifths of the bull's US$1,209.1m enterprise value, so a move in EV is a multiple in the equity. The associate add-back lifts the target from Rp135 (HOLD) to Rp187 (BUY) on a full write-off test, but the branch is solvent without it. What today's price implies: the target equals the Rp133 price at a 10.68% bull weight, against our 15%; the reverse DCF is unavailable because the base floors at zero across the plausible range [S0].
